restriction_type_key.occupancy-only: Limits WHO may occupy (local employment). Does not cap price or appreciation. Keeps a unit in the workforce; does not make it affordable to a target AMI.
restriction_type_key.price-capped: Caps resale price, usually at original price plus an index. Preserves affordability to a defined AMI band across resales. This is the shared-equity family.
restriction_type_key.unverified: Restriction mechanics not yet checked against a primary source.
restriction_type_key.n/a: Not a deed restriction (a fee, tax, loan or land holding).
restriction_type_key.either: The owner picks one of two restrictions when it is recorded: an occupancy-only one, or a price-capped one that pays more. Read the recorded deed to know which applies to a home.

key_programs.name: Housing Mitigation Program (Land Use Code Section 3-720)
key_programs.income_band_ami: Tier 1 (<=120% AMI) and Tier 2 (<=180% AMI) for new mitigation units
key_programs.summary: Development subject to the Land Use Code must provide or fund deed-restricted housing scaled to the employees it generates, with the required share varying by type of use; required square footage is assigned income tiers, and mitigation units carry fixed initial sale prices. Original developers cannot take appreciation and must sell at or below the initial sale price.
key_programs.magnitude: Mitigation = employee generation rate x 400 sq ft per employee x required percentage (40%-90% depending on use). If 2,000 sq ft or more is required, at least 50% of it must be Tier 1.
key_programs.source_label: Telluride Affordable Housing Guidelines, amended June 26, 2026 (Part 2); SMRHA 2025 Housing Needs Analysis

evidence.quote: The amount of required housing mitigation is calculated based on employee generation rate (calculated based on type of use) x 400 sq. ft. (gross floor area per employee) x required percentage mitigation (which ranges from 40%-90% depending on the type of use).

The Housing Mitigation Program governs Affordable Housing Units as defined in and required by Land Use Code, as may be amended, requiring developers to mitigate the housing impacts of certain types of development by concurrently creating or accommodating Affordable Housing.

Original Developers of Mitigation Unit are not eligible for appreciation or capital improvement increases, and are required to sell Mitigation Unit at or below the Initial Sale Price or Original Purchase Price indicated in the developer's Deed Restriction.
If 2,000 square feet or greater of Affordable Housing is required, at least fifty percent (50%) of the required square footage shall be designated Tier 1, and the remainder may be Tier 2.

key_programs.name: Payment-in-lieu (PIL) fee for housing mitigation
key_programs.summary: Where the Land Use Code allows it, developers can pay a per-square-foot fee instead of building mitigation housing. The fee equals the gap between average free-market and Tier 1 affordable sale prices per square foot, is recalculated each year, and goes into a dedicated affordable housing account.
key_programs.magnitude: Methodology example: $458 per sq ft on January 31, 2018. The current fee was not stated in the Guidelines.
key_programs.source_label: Telluride Affordable Housing Guidelines, amended June 26, 2026 (206.3 and Appendix C)

evidence.quote: Payment-in-lieu Fees – In certain cases the Land Use Code allows developers subject to housing mitigation requirements to make a payment-in-lieu of providing housing.
Payment-in-lieu fees are paid to the Town and held in an account dedicated to Affordable Housing.

The PIL fee is based on the difference between the market price of housing and the price that is affordable to Households with incomes that are targeted by the Telluride Affordable Housing Guidelines.
Based on this methodology, the Payment-in-Lieu Fee on January 31, 2018, was $458. For the current Payment-in-Lieu Fee, contact the Town Planning and Building Department.
